Hey guys,

I am starting to write an e-book on modern front-end development workflows and practices. It is aimed at beginners in front-end development but will go pretty in depth in terms of workflows. This isn't an advanced front-end development book, it's more for those who are designers, back-end devs, or people who are new to web development. Basically, I want to take a look at what it is like taking a website from the initial design to the completed project and show exactly how and what tools are used.

There are a lot of books that talk about HTML/CSS/JS but not very many that discuss actual workflows for front-end development while still focusing on the fundamental building blocks such as HTML and CSS. For example, tools like Git and Bower are great but you probably won't find very much info on them in a book on CSS or jQuery.

Warning - this doesn't work in Firefox

As PER the CSS standard Firefox ONLY support the use of content with the ::before,:before, ::after and :after pseudo selectors.

I think the reason for this is to allow you to inject additional content into a page (i.e. to give extra data) but not to change the existing content.

However Webkit browsers (Chrome, Chromium, Opera - maybe others) all let you apply the content property to any part of the DOM, Firefox only allows it to be applied :before and :after existing DOM elements.

In other words - webkit browsers let you CHANGE the existing page, Firefox only allows you to ADD content to the existing page. That seems much safer to me.

:before and :after are the CSS2 pseudo selectors

::before and ::after are the CSS3 versions (I think)
